speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether the Government has assessed the export potential of Singapore’s water recycling and integrated water management capabilities, particularly in regions facing rising industrial and digital infrastructure demand; and (b) whether there are plans to develop a coordinated strategy to position Singapore firms as global leaders in this sector.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Today, Singapore is globally recognised for our integrated water management and our know-how also creates opportunities for our companies to meet the needs of other countries.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Our biennial Singapore International Water Week has become one of the world’s leading conferences for public utilities and the water industry since its establishment in 2008.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It comprises flagship events that gather suppliers and customers of innovative water, coastal and flood solutions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Co-organised by PUB, the event culminates in the Lee Kuan Yew Water Prize.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Events like these help Singapore-based companies and startups gain visibility and access to potential investors, partners and customers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Our agencies also regularly organise business missions to and facilitate engagements with stakeholders in key regional markets.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These efforts have been particularly helpful for smaller companies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Hydroleap, a watertech company specialising in electrochemical separation, piloted its water recycling systems with Amazon Web Services (AWS) at a data centre facility in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It has since expanded to markets like Indonesia, Malaysia and Australia.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: SG Enviro, another Singapore startup focused on advanced water purification treatment using nano-bubble technology, has been working on water reclamation and wastewater treatment projects with palm oil refineries in Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They can also use those grants for development of their businesses and to set up their businesses overseas.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Companies which need financing for overseas expansion can also tap the Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS).

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They also can access trade loans for the buying and selling of goods.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We announced enhancements to some of these schemes at this year's Budget and the Ministry of Trade and Industry's Committee of Supply (MTI COS) session.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I want to ensure the Member that the Government will continue to support our local water tech companies, to strengthen their global competitiveness and better position them to pursue market opportunities abroad.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have different supplementary questions for Question Nos 5 and 6 respectively.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: For Question No 5, I would like to ask the Minister of State, will the Government consider a circular economy export office to specifically bundle our water recycling and waste to energy technologies, like Tuas Nexus, as a single high value export for the growing cities in ASEAN and beyond in Asia?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Is MTI actively marketing Singapore's integrated cooling plus water recycling solutions to regional digital hubs like Johor and Batam, to ensure our firms capture the spillover infrastructure demand from Singapore's own land constraint?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: For Question No 6, Mr Speaker, my supplementary questions are as follows.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: One, will MTI introduce a sovereign project bond or risk sharing mechanism that allows Singapore water firms to bid for larger scale overseas desalination projects with the financial backing of a, so called, Team Singapore guarantee?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Second supplementary question, will the Government allow for more export oriented test bedding within PUB facilities where the primary goal is not just local water security, but providing the firms with a globally recognised reference track to win overseas tenders?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to supporting Singapore water tech companies and to use our know-how to tap onto the opportunities outside of Singapore, I think those are very useful suggestions and important ones.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Allow me to put that into context; because I have two questions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I can go a little bit into detail to answer Mr Dennis Tan's questions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First of all, maybe I start with the export test bedding and talk about PUB's support.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: PUB, in fact, has opened up its water insulation for test bedding.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, they have this Living Lab fund which provides R&D funding.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, if you are a local company, for example, Hydroleap or SG Enviro, you are able to use some of these funds to test bed some of these innovative solutions, which if it works, then you can potentially use it in Singapore and then potentially export to different markets.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: PUB also has support schemes for companies and research institutions to then pilot and to validate these new tech, which could be applied for both industrial as well as municipal water needs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: What I thought is also very important, because the Member is asking about how Singapore water tech companies can better expand into the overseas markets, is this.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And since, then the water tech industry has grown quite significantly.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For the schemes, at MTI COS, we have enhanced some of these schemes to help these companies, not just water tech companies, but companies who want to expand overseas.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, we enhanced the Market Readiness Assistance grant.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, even if you are already in the market, you can continue to use that grant.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We have enhanced the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation grant, and we have also enhanced the EFS.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: All of these, put together, enables our companies to expand overseas.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I give a quick example to illustrate this point.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Because of the support from Enterprise Singapore and MTI, it is now able to use the Enterprise Development Grant funding to upgrade its water technologies, which I mentioned earlier on.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It is expanded to Thailand, for example, partnering with the Bangkok Industrial Gas, to provide smart water treatment solutions in PepsiCo Thailand.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, I thank the Member for his questions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are indeed looking at water as a strategic imperative, not just as an existential issue for Singapore, but also supporting our water tech companies to test bed, to validate their ideas to grow and then to expand beyond our shores.
